title: Exceptional restriction of a Verdier dual
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of schemes
[def-weil-closed-immersion], with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$.
Choose the small etale sites or the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; in the pro-etale case
assume that $j$ is quasi-compact, meaning that the inverse image of each
quasi-compact open is quasi-compact. Let $\Lambda_T$ be a sheaf of commutative
rings on the chosen site of $T$, and use $\Lambda_Z=i^{-1}\Lambda_T$ and
$\Lambda_U=j^{-1}\Lambda_T$ as coefficient sheaves. Write
$\mathcal D(W)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_W))$ for the ordinary unbounded
derived category of module sheaves
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].
Use the exact inverse images $i^*=i^{-1}$, $j^*=j^{-1}$ and the closed direct
image $Ri_*=i_*$, applied termwise to complexes. Suppose that $i_*$ has a
right adjoint $Ri^!:\mathcal D(T)\to\mathcal D(Z)$, that is, natural bijections
$\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,Ri^!L)$
for all $N\in\mathcal D(Z)$ and $L\in\mathcal D(T)$.

For any $\omega_T\in\mathcal D(T)$ fix
$\omega_Z=Ri^!\omega_T$, and put
$D_TK=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_T}(K,\omega_T)$ and
$D_ZM=R\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_Z}(M,\omega_Z)$, using the derived internal Hom
[def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for every $K\in\mathcal D(T)$ there is
a natural isomorphism
$$
\alpha_K:Ri^!D_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_Zi^*K.
$$
This assertion does not use biduality or require boundedness,
constructibility, or finite Tor amplitude of $K$ or $\omega_T$.

proof.text:
First establish the closed-support facts on module sheaves. On the pro-etale
site [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] applies to the sheaf of rings
$\Lambda_T$ and the quasi-compact $j$: $i_*$ is exact, its counit
$i^{-1}i_*\to\operatorname{id}$ is invertible, $j^{-1}i_*=0$, and
$0\to j_!j^{-1}F\to F\to i_*i^{-1}F\to0$ is exact. The last sequence shows
that $i^{-1}F=j^{-1}F=0$ implies $F=0$.
On the etale site [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identifies the stalk
of $i_*G$ at a point of $Z$ with the stalk of $G$. At a point of $U$ it is
zero: an etale neighbourhood inside $U$ has empty closed fibre, and the
module sheaf has zero sections on the empty scheme. Exactness and
conservativity of geometric stalks
[prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]
therefore imply exactness of $i_*$. The closed counit and supported essential
image are [lem-kun-04ca]; they give $j^{-1}i_*=0$ and joint detection by
$i^{-1},j^{-1}$. Indeed if $j^{-1}F=0$, its support is in $Z$, so
$F\cong i_*G$ and $i^{-1}F\cong G$; if the latter is zero, so is $F$.
These abelian-sheaf assertions apply to module sheaves: the canonical maps
respect the induced coefficient actions, and forgetting those actions
reflects exactness and isomorphisms.

The inverse-image functors on abelian sheaves are exact by
[lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. For the identified coefficient
sheaves, module pullback is inverse image: the tensor formula in
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] has inverse maps
$m\otimes a\mapsto am$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Thus module inverse image
is exact as well. Exactness of both $i^{-1}$ and $i_*$ lets their termwise
functors, unit, and counit descend through the localization at
quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the homotopy
adjunction and its triangle identities are
[lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. Hence
$i^{-1}\dashv Ri_*=i_*$ on the ordinary derived categories, and the closed
counit stays invertible. Since exact inverse image commutes with cohomology,
the joint detection in step 1 also detects acyclic complexes, by applying it
to every cohomology sheaf.
For $t=i,j$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives
$t^{-1}(P\otimes^L Q)\cong t^{-1}P\otimes^Lt^{-1}Q$ for arbitrary complexes,
with the relevant inverse-image coefficient rings; no Tor bound is used.

For arbitrary $N\in\mathcal D(Z)$ and $K\in\mathcal D(T)$, form the
projection morphism
$$c_{N,K}:i_*N\otimes^L K\longrightarrow i_*(N\otimes^Li^{-1}K)$$
as the adjoint, under step 2, of
$i^{-1}(i_*N\otimes^LK)\cong i^{-1}i_*N\otimes^Li^{-1}K
\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_N\otimes1}N\otimes^Li^{-1}K$.
Applying $i^{-1}$ to $c_{N,K}$ gives this isomorphism followed by the inverse
closed counit, so is invertible. Applying $j^{-1}$ gives the map between
zero objects, since $j^{-1}i_*=0$ and inverse image commutes with derived
tensor. Exact inverse image preserves mapping cones, since the termwise additive
functor preserves their direct sums and differential matrices. The cone of
$c_{N,K}$ therefore has both inverse images acyclic and is acyclic by
step 2. The morphism from the zero object to this cone induces an
isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf, hence is an isomorphism by
[lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The cone is a zero object,
so [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $c_{N,K}$ an isomorphism.
The construction is natural in $N,K$.

proof.text:
On either chosen ringed site, the currying isomorphism of
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives
$$R\mathcal Hom(P,R\mathcal Hom(Q,L))\cong R\mathcal Hom(P\otimes^LQ,L).$$
Taking $H^0$ of derived global sections and using
[lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on both sides gives the natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,R\mathcal Hom(Q,L))\cong
\operatorname{Hom}(P\otimes^LQ,L).$$
Both cited results apply to arbitrary objects of the ordinary unbounded
derived category of any small ringed site.

For every $N\in\mathcal D(Z)$, compose the assumed ambient exceptional
adjunction, step 4 on $T$, the inverse of step 3 inside Hom, the assumed
exceptional adjunction again, and step 4 on $Z$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,Ri^!D_TK)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N,D_TK)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*N\otimes^LK,\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(i_*(N\otimes^Li^*K),\omega_T)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N\otimes^Li^*K,Ri^!\omega_T)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N\otimes^Li^*K,\omega_Z)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,D_Zi^*K).
\end{aligned}
$$
This is a bijection natural in the arbitrary test object $N$, and
contravariantly natural in $K$. All its objects lie in their specified
ambient categories; neither a constructible adjunction nor a finite-Tor
projection formula is being substituted for an ambient one.

source.place: Proof, displayed Hom chain; all arrows separated and justified by steps 2-4 and the stated ambient adjunction

proof.text:
Write $B=Ri^!D_TK$, $C=D_Zi^*K$, and let
$\theta_N:\operatorname{Hom}(N,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(N,C)$ be step 5.
Set $\alpha_K=\theta_B(1_B)$ and $\gamma_K=\theta_C^{-1}(1_C)$.
Naturality in $N$ gives $\theta_N(f)=\alpha_Kf$ and
$\theta_N^{-1}(g)=\gamma_Kg$; the inverse composites give
$\gamma_K\alpha_K=1_B$ and $\alpha_K\gamma_K=1_C$.
Naturality of $\theta$ in $K$ gives naturality of $\alpha$.
The tensor-Hom transposes use evaluation and the exceptional transposes use
the adjunction counit, so this is the canonical evaluation-defined
comparison in the source. Yoneda is applied directly to the two objects in
$\mathcal D(Z)$; no localization to etale test objects and no biduality is
needed.

split_report.summary: Second reading replaced the misapplied constructible fix-node citations by ambient ringed-site facts. Explicitly bound sites, inverse-image coefficient rings, all ambient complexes and the exceptional adjunction; restored the missing quasi-compact-complement hypothesis on the pro-etale side. Proved the closed projection identity by inverse-image counit and open-closed detection, derived the tensor-Hom bijection from the existing ringed-site currying and global-Hom theorems, and wrote the Hom chain and Yoneda inverse in six steps. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the sole proof paragraph of the original blueprint item: steps 1-3 justify its middle projection identity, step 4 justifies its two tensor-Hom arrows, step 5 gives its Hom chain, and step 6 expands Yoneda and naturality. Retains the conditional ambient route without biduality. The unit is finite-stage geometric biduality; the explicit pro-etale complement condition holds for its finite-type schemes.
split_report.off_unit_tools: The ringed-site tensor pullback, internal-Hom calculus, global-Hom, exact inverse image and termwise adjunction statements are generic tools. The etale closed-support and geometric-stalk statements and the ringed pro-etale open-closed statement supply the exact closed-site infrastructure. These are used as black boxes with exactly their stated domains; no tool_uses maintainer field is set.

tool_uses.why: Step 1 uses only the generic small-etale closed-immersion fully faithful pushforward, its inverse-image counit, and its supported essential image. These are ringed-site infrastructure for the formal closed-costalk comparison; no theorem in this unit supplies them, and this use does not replace its geometric biduality route.
